content.text: Direct correction combined with metalinguistic explanation was favoured most often (215/447 responses, 48.10%), ahead of direct correction alone (111/447, 24.83%) (Liu & Wu, 2019). Preferences also varied by proficiency: at the lower level, 7 of 8 students wanted feedback solely from teachers, whereas at the higher level, 5 of 6 preferred feedback from both teachers and peers (Liu & Wu, 2019). The evidence suggests that learner beliefs are proficiency-sensitive, though the non-randomised, single-programme design limits generalisability.

uncitedSentences.sentence: Automated writing evaluation (AWE) introduces a distinct revision dynamic.

content.text: Automated writing evaluation (AWE) introduces a distinct revision dynamic. Zhang and Hyland (2018) documented contrasting engagement profiles: one learner resubmitted an essay 13 times and raised her score from 79 to 90, while another resubmitted once and spent under 14 minutes on the task. Teacher feedback addressed more error types (16) than AWE feedback (8), though assignment differences may have confounded this comparison (Zhang & Hyland, 2018). Students reported spending more time revising after AWE feedback (6.2 hours) than after peer (5.8) or teacher feedback (4.7), and 88% submitted more than five times (Zhang & Hyland, 2021). This case study's single-classroom scope limits generalisability (Zhang & Hyland, 2021).
